contradictions.detail: The listing says the clean Ohio title describes the car as a '911SE', while the production certificate and listing identify it as a 1979 911SC coupe.

critical_evidence.evidence: No engine rebuild is claimed. Carrera chain tensioners and Turbo valve covers are stated as 'the seller tells us', with no invoice cited. There is no mention of head stud (Dilavar) inspection or replacement, which is the key SC weakness. The March 2023 valve adjustment and gaskets are dated in the listing.
Compression results and borescope images are said to be in the gallery but were not examined here. No leakdown test is mentioned.
Only a rear underside shot of the heat exchangers and transaxle is attached. The front pan, battery boxes, kidney bowls, floors, torsion tube ends and shock towers were not examined here.

A Porsche Production Specifications certificate is photographed (930/04 engine, 915/61 transmission, P5 GP White, black partial leather). No photos of stamped engine or transaxle numbers, and matching numbers are not claimed.

1979 is not smog-exempt in CA (1976+). The listing states the smog pump, air injectors and catalytic converter were removed, so the car would fail the CA visual inspection until the equipment is reinstalled. CARB status of the Dansk heat exchangers is also unknown.

documentation.rationale: Identity half is good: chassis number, a photographed production certificate, a clean title (model mis-described) and dated work entries. Maintenance half is incomplete: records, compression sheet and borescope images are not examined here. The tensioner upgrade is seller-stated only, nothing addresses head studs, true mileage is unknown after the odometer repair, and there are no front underbody photos.

condition.rationale: Disclosed cosmetic faults: decklid ding, body chips, driver bolster wear (visible), headliner stains, and A/C removed. Positives are recent dated work (2023 valve adjustment, gaskets, return lines, tires, spring plates). Engine internals, studs, leaks and rust are unproven either way.

price_value.rationale: No fair value or comps are supplied. Bidding already sits at $30,000 with seven days left, and a likely hammer is above the budget's max price. Known work to restore CA emissions equipment adds cost, and actual mileage is unknown.

mission_fit.rationale: An analog manual coupe fits the keeper brief in principle. But the likely price conflicts with cash preservation in accelerated_bridge mode, and the car needs emissions restoration before it can be registered in CA.

logistics.rationale: Ohio remote auction with no stated PPI arrangement before close. CA registration requires reinstalling the smog equipment. The seller's offer of more videos helps only modestly.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Grand Prix White non-sunroof coupe with a 915 manual, Fuchs wheels and a factory certificate is a desirable spec. It is diluted by the A/C removal, the stereo/subwoofer install and the emissions delete, and numbers are unconfirmed.

evidence.mission_note: As an analog GP White manual coupe this matches the keeper brief, but at the likely auction price it is attractive only as a keeper and conflicts with cash preservation while the household runs on one car. It also needs emissions restoration before it can be registered in CA.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the chassis number matches a photographed production certificate listing a 930/04 engine, 915/61 gearbox, Grand Prix White and black partial leather, and the clean Ohio title has a model mis-description. It documents dated 2022–2023 work (valve adjustment, valve cover gaskets, oil return lines, shift coupler, tires, spring plates) and provides compression and borescope images, though those were not examined here. Observed issues are an odometer repaired in 2022 so true mileage is unknown, a 2005 front-end respray of unstated cause, cosmetic chips, a decklid ding, seat and headliner wear, the A/C removed, and the catalytic converter and smog pump deleted on a car CA requires to pass smog. The SC's key risks remain open: the Carrera tensioner upgrade is a seller statement without an invoice, head studs are not addressed, no leakdown is given, and the front pan and floors are not shown. Bidding is already at $30,000 with seven days left, and no comps or fair value were supplied.
